description: Python dependency files that do not have a sibling uv.lock yet, so the python-dependency-audit CI job does not audit them. infra/test/ci/pythonDependencyLocks.test.ts fails a Python dependency file (pyproject.toml, requirements*.txt/.in/.lock, Pipfile, setup.py with install_requires) the audit does not cover unless it is listed here with a reason and the change that will add the lock. Remove an entry when its uv.lock lands; the test fails an entry whose path is gone or already has a uv.lock. rangedInputs lists the hand-written, ranged files of a published package that sit beside its uv.lock on purpose: the ranges are the published install contract, so they are not uv exports. The audit skips them, the test checks each entry still exists beside a uv.lock, and the lock resolves the same ranges.

rangedInputs.reason: Ranged install requirements of the published VamsCLI package, mirrored from pyproject.toml and setup.py by tests/test_packaging_manifests.py. They stay ranges because users install the package with them; tools/VamsCLI/uv.lock resolves the same ranges.
Ranged development requirements of VamsCLI, the same ranges as the dev extra in pyproject.toml; tools/VamsCLI/uv.lock resolves them.
The build tools pyproject.toml's [build-system] requires, ranged as there. They are the build dependency group of tools/VamsCLI/uv.lock, which requirements.lock is exported from.
setuptools install_requires of the published VamsCLI package, mirroring its ranged pyproject.toml dependencies; tools/VamsCLI/uv.lock resolves the same ranges.

exemptions.reason: Upstream-owned: the Splat Toolbox sync copies upstream's container/requirements.txt over this file on every cdk synth, so it cannot be a uv export. The image is upstream's Dockerfile, which does not install it; only the pipeline test runner does.
boto3 and botocore for the Splat Toolbox utils package; no Dockerfile installs it, and a uv project beside the upstream-owned requirements.txt is not possible.

Installed into Isaac Sim's bundled Python, which a lock must target explicitly. Draft PR #1736 (#1669, Isaac Lab 6.x) rewrites this file and the Dockerfile, so it moves to a uv project after that PR merges.

Hash-locked pip-compile output (`uv pip compile --generate-hashes`) that the Dockerfile installs into Isaac Sim's bundled Python; it is not a uv.lock, so the CI audit does not read it until the image moves to a uv project. Draft PR #1736 (#1669, Isaac Lab 6.x) rewrites this file and the Dockerfile, so it moves to a uv project after that PR merges.
